newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian farm union pushes for coffee/cocoa reform.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian farm union pushes for coffee/cocoa reform.

text.p: Donor-sponsored reforms of Ivory Coast's Caistab commodities board are needed to ensure benefits reach cocoa and coffee farmers, an Ivorian farmers union said.

The Syndicat National des Agriculteurs de Cote d'Ivoire (SYNAGCI) said in a statement it supported wide-sweeping reforms which would end "reference" farmgate prices, prices for marketing stages from farms to ports, and forward sales of about two-thirds of each season's crop by the Caistab.

"The disappearance of these elements signals clearly the removal from the Caistab of its prerogatives, which would mean its dismantlement," the statement said. "The reforms undertaken will be completed and have the support of genuine cocoa and coffee farmers."

Ivory Coast and donors will hold talks on August 8-15 to consider agricultural reforms under a $150 million World Bank loan dating to 1995 during wider talks on setting a three-year economic policy plan.
Donors say further liberalisation of marketing and a reduced role for the Caistab would mean higher farmgate cocoa and coffee prices for farmers.
The Caistab, which used to exert a monopoly over all stages of cocoa and coffee marketing, has already loosened its grip on marketing since 1995, passing some functions over to the private sector.
Ivorian farmers receive about 40 percent of FOB cocoa prices, one of the lowest rates in the world, compared to up to 85 percent at times in countries like Indonesia.
The talks in August will also bring together World Bank, IMF and IMF officials to discuss an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility for Ivory Coast.
